Based on the search results, here's information about the pdf.js getTextContent API and TextContent items:

## getTextContent API Overview

The `getTextContent()` method returns a promise that is resolved with a TextContent object that represents the page's text content.

## TextContent Items Structure

The TextContent object contains an `items` array, where each item represents information about a small piece of text on the page. From the items of TextContent, you can obtain the coordinates and text information of the text.

## Accessing Items

To access the text content items, you can iterate through the `items` array:

The `textContent.items` array contains individual items, and each item has a `str` property that contains the text string.

## Example Usage

A typical pattern for extracting text would be:
```javascript
const page = await pdf.getPage(pageNumber);
const textContent = await page.getTextContent();
const pageText = textContent.items.map((item) => item.str).join(" ");
```

**Note:** All occurrences of whitespace will be replaced by standard spaces (0x20).

For complete API documentation, you can refer to the official Mozilla PDF.js API documentation at mozilla.github.io/pdf.js.

**Error Handling:** A try-catch block manages any exceptions during the loading process.

A streaming variant `streamTextContent(params) → ReadableStream` carries the same note ([PDFPageProxy API docs](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/api/draft/module-pdfjsLib-PDFPageProxy.html)).

**Shapes**, verbatim from the JSDoc in `src/display/api.js`:

- `getTextContentParameters`: `includeMarkedContent` — "When true include marked content items in the items array of TextContent. The default is `false`"; `disableNormalization` — "When true the text is *not* normalized in the worker-thread. The default is `false`."
- `TextContent`: `items: Array<TextItem | TextMarkedContent>`, `styles: Object<string, TextStyle>` ("indexed by font name"), `lang: string | null` ("The document /Lang attribute").
- `TextItem`: `str` (text content), `dir` ("'ttb', 'ltr' or 'rtl'"), `transform` (transformation matrix), `width`/`height` ("in device space"), `fontName` ("Font name used by PDF.js for converted font"), `hasEOL` ("Indicating if the text content is followed by a line-break").
- `TextMarkedContent`: `type` ('beginMarkedContent' | 'beginMarkedContentProps' | 'endMarkedContent') and `id`.

([src/display/api.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js))

**The canonical non-browser pattern**, verbatim from the official example — note that `url` is passed a filesystem path, and that resources are explicitly released:

```js
import { getDocument } from "pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs";
const loadingTask = getDocument({ url: pdfPath });
// per page:
const { items } = await pdfPage.getTextContent();
console.log(items.map(item => item.str).join(" "));
```

with `pdfPage.cleanup()` after each page and `loadingTask.destroy()` at the end ([examples/node/getinfo.mjs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs)).

Text extraction is the part of PDF.js least entangled with the DOM: it needs the worker/parsing path but not canvas. That last sentence is **inference**, though well-supported by the fact that the canvas factory is only reached via rendering, not `getTextContent`.

## 3. Runtime assumptions that affect Bun — the documented facts

Everything hinges on one predicate, `isNodeJS` in `src/shared/util.js`:

```js
const isNodeJS =
  (typeof PDFJSDev === "undefined" || PDFJSDev.test("GENERIC")) &&
  typeof process === "object" &&
  process + "" === "[object process]" &&
  !process.versions.nw &&
  !(process.versions.electron && process.type && process.type !== "browser");
```

([src/shared/util.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/shared/util.js)). It is a **duck-type on `process`'s string tag**, with no `process.versions.node` check and no acknowledgement of alternative runtimes.

That single flag then drives, in `src/display/api.js` ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js)):

| Assumption | Documented behavior |
|---|---|
| Workers | `if (isNodeJS) { this.#isWorkerDisabled = true; GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc ||= … }`, with the comment "Workers aren't supported in Node.js, force-disabling them there." Otherwise it does `new Worker(workerSrc, { type: "module" })` and falls back to `_setupFakeWorkerGlobal` (worker code loaded into the main thread via dynamic import) on failure. |
| Canvas / filters / data | `PDFJSDev.test("GENERIC") && isNodeJS ? NodeCanvasFactory : DOMCanvasFactory`, likewise `NodeFilterFactory` and `NodeBinaryDataFactory`. |
| Font handling | `disableFontFace` defaults to `isNodeJS`; `useSystemFonts` defaults to `!isNodeJS && !disableFontFace`. |
| Image APIs | `isOffscreenCanvasSupported` and `isImageDecoderSupported` both default to `!isNodeJS`. |

And in `node_utils.js` ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js)), the Node path assumes three more things:

1. **`process.getBuiltinModule` exists.** It is used three times: `process.getBuiltinModule("module").createRequire(import.meta.url)` in the polyfill block and again inside `NodeCanvasFactory._createCanvas`, and `process.getBuiltinModule("fs/promises")` inside `fetchData`. Only the first is wrapped in `try/catch` (`warn("Cannot access the \`require\` function: …")`); the two in `fetchData` and `_createCanvas` are unguarded.
2. **Data URLs are filesystem paths.** `fetchData(url)` is literally `fs.readFile(url)`, so in the Node branch `getDocument({ url })` reads from disk rather than over HTTP.
3. **Globals may be overwritten.** `globalThis.DOMMatrix` and `globalThis.Path2D` are assigned from `@napi-rs/canvas` if absent (with `warn("Cannot polyfill \`DOMMatrix\`, rendering may be broken.")` otherwise), and `if (!globalThis.navigator?.language) globalThis.navigator = { language: "en-US", platform: "", userAgent: "" }`. `@napi-rs/canvas` is `require`d optionally — missing it only warns.

## 4. What this implies for Bun — inference, not documentation

PDF.js's behavior under Bun is entirely determined by whether Bun satisfies `process + "" === "[object process]"`, and **I was not able to verify that from an authoritative source** — treat this as the open question:

- **If Bun passes the check** (`isNodeJS === true`): workers are force-disabled, so parsing runs on the main thread via the fake worker regardless of Bun's native `Worker` support; `getDocument({ url })` hits `fs.readFile`; and the `process.getBuiltinModule` calls in `fetchData`/`_createCanvas` must work or they throw uncaught. Bun's docs mark `node:process` as "mostly implemented" and list only `sourceMapsEnabled` and `addUncaughtExceptionCaptureCallback` as missing — `getBuiltinModule` is neither confirmed nor listed as absent ([Bun Node API compat](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/nodejs-apis)). A third-party bug report claims `process.getBuiltinModule` is `undefined` under Bun alongside `DOMMatrix` errors ([pdf-parse#73](https://github.com/mehmet-kozan/pdf-parse/issues/73)) — that is **weak evidence** (downstream wrapper, unverified, possibly an older Bun), and it **conflicts** with Bun's own compat page. I'd want to confirm it with `bun -e 'console.log(typeof process.getBuiltinModule)'` before relying on either claim.
- **If Bun fails the check** (`isNodeJS === false`): PDF.js takes the browser path — `DOMCanvasFactory`, `DOMBinaryDataFactory` (fetch-based, so a bare filesystem path in `url` would not resolve), `disableFontFace` defaults to `false`, `isOffscreenCanvasSupported`/`isImageDecoderSupported` default to `true`, and a real `new Worker(workerSrc, { type: "module" })` is attempted. None of the `node_utils.js` polyfills would run.

Two further practical inferences that follow from documented facts: (a) since the official example and the in-code warning both point at `legacy/build/pdf.mjs`, that is the build to use under Bun as well — the modern build's Node branch does nothing but warn; and (b) for **text extraction specifically**, `@napi-rs/canvas`, `DOMMatrix` and `Path2D` should not be needed, so the canvas warnings are likely benign for that use case — but PDF.js does not document this guarantee anywhere I found, so verify it against your own PDFs rather than assuming it.

**Bottom line on evidence quality:** parts 1 and 2 are directly documented and I'd rely on them. Part 3 is directly readable in current `master` source. Part 4 is reasoning from that source; no official PDF.js source makes any claim about Bun, and the one Bun-specific data point I found is third-party and contradicted by Bun's own docs.
